title: Pentagon asked the Baltic states to tone down warnings about Russia
summary: Reuters, citing three European officials and one US official, reports that Pentagon officials including policy chief Elbridge Colby asked Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and others in recent weeks to moderate public statements about the Russian threat. One example cited was Estonian PM Kristen Michal calling Putin a rat in a corner. The Pentagon said it won't comment on private conversations; the Baltic defence ministries did not respond.
corroboration: One original report (Reuters). Dozens of outlets repeated it, which adds reach, not corroboration.
analysis: Credible outlet and several sources, but nothing on the record yet. A European official quoted by Reuters pointed out the irony: Baltic intelligence services have been among the calmer voices. It fits the US push for a negotiated end to the war that includes sanctions relief for Russia. Watch for on-the-record Baltic responses.

title: NATO's top commander in Latvia: the threat is real, but no need to dramatise
summary: General Alexus Grynkewich, NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe, told journalists in Latvia that Russia's war in Ukraine shows its willingness to use force, that the alliance is already prepared for existing threats, and that resilience and preparedness are what matter.
corroboration: Reported by LETA and Baltic outlets.
analysis: Calm but vigilant, in line with Baltic intelligence assessments. Notable that NATO's military leadership and the Pentagon's political message point in the same direction this week.

title: German brigade starts electronic surveillance of Kaliningrad and Belarus
summary: The head of the Bundeswehr's Cyber and Information Domain Command told Reuters on 28 October that about 170 electronic-warfare personnel are deployed in Lithuania from 23 October to 7 December, intercepting signals to give early warning of military activity in Kaliningrad and Belarus.
corroboration: Reuters, confirmed by Bundeswehr and a German state ministry.
analysis: Strengthens NATO's early-warning picture right where this briefing has the least visibility. It also means that in future, 'nothing reported' from this sector carries more weight.

title: Sabotage arrests in Germany, Poland and Romania
summary: Munich prosecutors say two Belarusian men, aged 39 and 50, have been in custody since 7 October for plotting to set fire to infrastructure near Nuremberg on behalf of a foreign power, for payment. Der Spiegel, citing security sources, says that power is Russia. Romania links the same men to the 14 September arson at a Brașov defence plant; a Ukrainian was arrested in Warsaw.
corroboration: Prosecutors, Romanian intelligence and several independent outlets.
analysis: Prosecutors did not name Russia; the attribution comes from security sources and Romania's intelligence service. The pattern, cheap recruits from third countries paid for one-off jobs, matches the Leipzig drone case that Germany formally blamed on Russian military intelligence. Moscow denies all such accusations.

title: Fourth Russian cargo ship loads armour at Baltiysk
summary: Satellite images from 23 October show the cargo ship Lady R at the Baltiysk naval base with armoured and logistics vehicles waiting to load, after three other ships loaded similar equipment on 15–16 October.
corroboration: Two OSINT groups; reported by Ukrainian and Russian independent outlets.
analysis: The loading is documented, the destination is not. These sanctioned ships have previously supplied Russia's Africa Corps via Tobruk in Libya. Equipment leaving Kaliningrad would reduce local capacity, not build it up. Videos framing this as a Kaliningrad invasion go well beyond the evidence.

title: Russia's mobilization: no decree, but call-ups never stopped
summary: Foreign Policy argues that Russia has been legally mobilized since 2022 and has run a year-round draft since January, so a new announcement may never come. CNN reports coercive recruitment of vulnerable men.
analysis: Earlier Ukrainian predictions of a formal mobilization from October have not come true as a decree. The manpower appears to go to the Ukraine front. No sign of new units being formed toward the Baltic direction.
